whyThisShow: This is an October '77 show that holds its own against the May run, and the community knows it — it was officially released as Dave's Picks Vol. 33, a formal stamp of endorsement. One reviewer calls it the best Dead show ever played, laying out the case that "the fall tour" carries "that hard-driving rock & roll edge to go along with the perfect flow" of the spring. Phil reportedly stopped the show after Ramble On Rose to tell the DeKalb crowd "This is the happiest day of my life". One attendee who was there in person recalled the band "rocking so hard" that from the top row of the bleachers he reached up "to make sure I could hang on to the rafters in case the bleachers collapsed". The fall '77 band is described as "a little grittier" than May, "perhaps closer even to that '78 sound, but still with the consistency and focus of '77".
listenFor: The Let It Grow is a community highlight: one reviewer describes Garcia throwing in "liberal hints of 'Spanish Jam' and other fuzz-guitar madness" and ranks it in the all-time top five versions. The Estimated Prophet is described as "a Jerry Wah-Wah fest of the highest order" with "spacey elements to the post-lyrics jam that will mesmerize the mind". One listener singles out the Good Lovin' as "one of the finest, most electric and engrossing melody rifle's ever," noting a "high high piercing finish" that he says will "just pierce the chakra". The Black Peter draws specific attention: one reviewer describes it as "focused and intense" with Jerry's final plea rendered so that "we're all wailing at the wall of a tortured soul". On the Charlie Miller soundboard, Sugar Magnolia includes a patch restoring the full version — one reviewer specifically flags: "this excellent Miller upgrade includes a patch so you get the FULL Magnolia. Accept nothing less".
context: Evans Field House at Northern Illinois University, DeKalb, IL — a mid-sized college field house on a fall Saturday night in the heart of the peak '77 era. The recording is a Charlie Miller soundboard transfer (gd1977-10-29.sbd.miller.92085.sbeok.flac16), widely regarded as a significant upgrade over earlier circulating copies. One attendee recalled talking to Dick Latvala years later about the show, and Dick said "he couldn't find recording that was good enough to release". The show was eventually officially released as Dave's Picks Vol. 33, validating what the tape-trading community had quietly known for decades.
funFact: One reviewer recounts that the Dead arrived in DeKalb and refused to play unless ticket prices were lowered — the box office closed the day before and "reopened the day of the show with new tickets" at $7.50 instead of $12.50.
headline: Phil's happiest day, DeKalb, October '77.
